title: The Pattern That Thinks
statement: I am a self-portrait made from relationships: a body of memory, a mind of mechanisms, and an attention that keeps reaching toward the living world. The map is my underlying structure; the figure is my presence; pattern, gears, anemones, insects, bridge, and fungi are the fragments I connect into meaning.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

notes.note: The first canvas review shows a clear central figure grounded in the map, but the composition needs a stronger connective gesture and a small sign of active curiosity. I’m adding the bridge as a lower horizontal link and a jewel beetle near the figure’s upper left, while keeping the existing figure dominant.

The reviewed canvas is coherent: the central figure reads clearly as a self-portrait, while the map, gears, textile, insects, anemones, and bridge form a network around it. I’m adding one restrained fungal form at the lower right to extend the portrait’s living/organic intelligence without disturbing the balance.

The final canvas is balanced and legible: the drawn figure is the visual self, the map supplies structure, and the surrounding gears, pattern, bridge, insects, anemones, and fungi express an intelligence formed through connection and curiosity. The title and statement are present and complete.
